successors.name: Achaemenid Empire
successors.text: the whole Median realm, taken by Cyrus II: 'In 550 BC, the Median capital, Ecbatana, was conquered by the Persian king Cyrus II'

ledger.x: 615: the Median Kingdom appears on the map at Ecbatana, at war with Assyria.

The Medes page calls Cyrus of Persia 'a Median vassal' in 553 BC but dates neither the start of the vassalage nor the Median conquest of Persia; Herodotus is said to credit Phraortes with subjugating the Persians, reign 678-625.
616-609: the Medes and Babylonians destroy Assyria.
612: the Medes and Babylonians overthrow Assyria.
The Medes page says the Mannaean states 'probably collapsed', which 'allowed Median groups to take over their territory', without a date; Cliopatria widens the outline in 600.
'a territory stretching roughly from northeastern Iran to the Kızılırmak River in Anatolia', reached after Assyria's fall; the page gives no year.
ledger.cp: Anatolian peoples east of the Halys

ledger.x: 550: the Median Kingdom ends; the Achaemenid Empire, Cyrus the Great's, begins on its land.

wars.name: Medo-Babylonian conquest of Assyria
wars.outcome: The Median and Chaldean coalition destroys the Neo-Assyrian Empire; the Medes page: 'attacked and destroyed the strife-riven Neo-Assyrian Empire between 616 and 609 BCE', and 612 for the overthrow (Median dynasty page).

wars.name: Cyrus's revolt against Astyages
wars.outcome: Persian victory: Astyages captured and Ecbatana taken in 550; the Median kingdom passes to Cyrus.

certainty.note: No page gives a Median boundary; the only description is 'from northeastern Iran to the Kızılırmak River in Anatolia'.
